classification.difficultyReason: Coordinate factorisation, intercepts, the midpoint of the zeroes and substitution to construct six complete parabola sketches, including negative leading coefficients.

content.prompt: Use factoring to find the zeroes of each quadratic function. Hence sketch the graph of $y=f(x)$, showing all intercepts and the coordinates of the vertex.

answer.short: Zeroes: $-3,3$. Intercepts: $(-3,0)$, $(3,0)$ and $(0,-9)$. Vertex: $(0,-9)$; axis: $x=0$; concave up.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=(x-3)(x+3)\\f(0)&=-9\end{align*}$$
For the zeroes, $(x-3)(x+3)=0$, so $x=-3$ or $x=3$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-3+3}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=0\\f(0)&=-9\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(0,-9)$. The positive coefficient of $x^2$ gives a concave-up parabola through $(-3,0)$, $(3,0)$ and $(0,-9)$.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch with both x-intercepts and the vertex, which is also the y-intercept.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2-9; zeroes -3 and 3; vertex (0,-9); concave up.

answer.short: Zeroes: $-5,1$. Intercepts: $(-5,0)$, $(1,0)$ and $(0,-5)$. Vertex: $(-2,-9)$; axis: $x=-2$; concave up.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=(x+5)(x-1)\\f(0)&=-5\end{align*}$$
For the zeroes, $(x+5)(x-1)=0$, so $x=-5$ or $x=1$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-5+1}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=-2\\f(-2)&=(-2+5)(-2-1)\\f(-2)&=-9\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-2,-9)$. The positive coefficient of $x^2$ gives a concave-up parabola through $(-5,0)$, $(1,0)$ and $(0,-5)$.

spec.description: Complete parabola with intercept labels, dashed axis-to-vertex guide and vertex coordinates.

answer.short: Zeroes: $-6,2$. Intercepts: $(-6,0)$, $(2,0)$ and $(0,-12)$. Vertex: $(-2,-16)$; axis: $x=-2$; concave up.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=(x+6)(x-2)\\f(0)&=-12\end{align*}$$
For the zeroes, $(x+6)(x-2)=0$, so $x=-6$ or $x=2$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-6+2}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=-2\\f(-2)&=(-2+6)(-2-2)\\f(-2)&=-16\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-2,-16)$. The positive coefficient of $x^2$ gives a concave-up parabola through $(-6,0)$, $(2,0)$ and $(0,-12)$.

spec.description: Complete concave-up sketch with both roots, y-intercept, vertex and dashed symmetry guide.

answer.short: Zeroes: $0,4$. Intercepts: $(0,0)$ and $(4,0)$. Vertex: $(2,4)$; axis: $x=2$; concave down.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=x(4-x)\\f(0)&=0\end{align*}$$
For the zeroes, $x(4-x)=0$, so $x=0$ or $x=4$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{0+4}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=2\\f(2)&=2(4-2)\\f(2)&=4\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(2,4)$. The negative coefficient of $x^2$ gives a concave-down parabola through $(0,0)$ and $(4,0)$. The origin is both an $x$-intercept and the $y$-intercept.

answer.short: Zeroes: $-1,3$. Intercepts: $(-1,0)$, $(3,0)$ and $(0,3)$. Vertex: $(1,4)$; axis: $x=1$; concave down.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=-(x^2-2x-3)\\f(x)&=-(x+1)(x-3)\\f(0)&=3\end{align*}$$
For the zeroes, $-(x+1)(x-3)=0$, so $x=-1$ or $x=3$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-1+3}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=1\\f(1)&=-(1+1)(1-3)\\f(1)&=4\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(1,4)$. The negative coefficient of $x^2$ gives a concave-down parabola through $(-1,0)$, $(3,0)$ and $(0,3)$.

spec.description: Complete concave-down sketch with both x-intercepts, y-intercept and vertex coordinates.

answer.short: Zeroes: $-4,2$. Intercepts: $(-4,0)$, $(2,0)$ and $(0,8)$. Vertex: $(-1,9)$; axis: $x=-1$; concave down.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=-(x^2+2x-8)\\f(x)&=-(x+4)(x-2)\\f(0)&=8\end{align*}$$
For the zeroes, $-(x+4)(x-2)=0$, so $x=-4$ or $x=2$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-4+2}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=-1\\f(-1)&=-(-1+4)(-1-2)\\f(-1)&=9\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-1,9)$. The negative coefficient of $x^2$ gives a concave-down parabola through $(-4,0)$, $(2,0)$ and $(0,8)$.

spec.description: Complete concave-down sketch with both roots, y-intercept, dashed symmetry guide and vertex coordinates.
